archetype.name: Dual-Threat (efficiency-first)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose legs remain a real weapon but whose value this season came mostly from the pocket, posting the league's best yards per attempt and adjusted yards per dropback on modest volume, with scrambles bailing out broken plays.

report.headline: League-best yards per dropback, then thumb surgery: Jackson's season is on hold.
report.take:
Jackson is on injured reserve after thumb surgery. His coach puts the absence at 6-to-10 weeks, and the estimated return date is December 27. Before that, he was playing some of the most efficient football of his career. His 9.97 yards per attempt and 10.63 adjusted net yards per dropback both rank first among 54 qualifiers, his 0.313 EPA per dropback ranks third, and his 8.29 CPOE ranks third. Against last season, his completion rate and CPOE are each up 6.5 points and his yards per attempt is up 1.53. That is a clear rebound from a 2025 in which his EPA per play slipped to 20th and his win rate fell below .500.

The raw totals understate him because he barely played in two of his five games. Week 4 ended at 52% of snaps, and his Week 8 appearance at Buffalo was one incompletion on 2% of snaps before Tyler Huntley and later Joe Fagnano took over. That cameo is why his last-three-game passing yards per game read 57.4 below his season mark. The rates over the same stretch went up, not down: 0.467 EPA per dropback and a 10.2 CPOE. In the three full games he finished, he produced 9.2, 3.2 and 10.3 passing EPA, then 10.2 more in half a game against Tennessee. The low volume (19.4 attempts a game) reflects a run-leaning offense and lopsided early scripts, not a passer the team didn't trust.

The success is broad rather than one hot split. Throws under 10 air yards completed at 82% for 0.37 EPA, and throws of 10-plus yards produced 0.642 EPA per attempt. Zay Flowers turned 20 targets into 1.146 EPA per target. Some of this will cool. A CPOE above 8 is well beyond anything on his career line, where his best was 4.552 in 2024, and the deep and intermediate numbers rest on 18 and 16 attempts. The weak spots are third down and the red zone, plus a sack rate (6.7%, 23rd) that has been a problem since 2023. That is partly the cost of a quarterback who holds the ball 3.11 seconds hunting for something better behind a line ranked 24th in hit rate allowed.

Where it goes is mostly a calendar question. If the December estimate holds, Jackson returns for, at most, the final regular-season stretch. He would be coming back from surgery on a thumb whose hand the dossier does not specify, and that matters a great deal for a passer whose game this year was precision. The skill level looked real and consistent with his 2019 and 2024 peaks. The open question is how much of it survives the layoff.

strengths.title: Best per-throw efficiency in the league
strengths.body: He leads all qualifiers in yards per attempt and adjusted net yards per dropback while completing passes well above expectation. That comes from accuracy at every level rather than one schemed concept, and it continues the 2024 form (8.8 YPA, 2nd) more than the dip of 2025. The exact CPOE will likely regress on a larger sample, but top-five efficiency is consistent with his best seasons.

strengths.title: Real value beyond 10 air yards
strengths.body: Throws of 10-plus air yards returned 0.642 EPA per attempt, and the deep shots alone added 11.7 EPA. This is despite a 44.4% completion rate deep, which is normal for those throws. Flowers was the engine at 1.146 EPA per target. The samples are small, but the profile fits a quarterback whose extra time in the pocket gives routes time to develop.

strengths.title: Scrambles as a pressure valve
strengths.body: Designed runs were rare (six), but he scrambled on 8.9% of dropbacks for 0.419 EPA each and six first downs out of ten. That keeps his rushing at 28.8 yards a game (6th among QBs) even as the team asks him to run less than in his peak years. It also pays back part of the sack cost of holding the ball.

concerns.title: Availability is the whole story now
concerns.body: Thumb surgery has him on IR with a 6-to-10-week timetable, and he is listed fourth on the depth chart. This continues a pattern: he played 12, 12 and 13 games in three of the past five seasons. The return date is an estimate. Even an on-time return comes with rust and the open question of how the thumb affects his throwing.

concerns.title: Sacks from holding the ball
concerns.body: His 6.7% sack rate ranks 23rd, and 28% of his pressures became sacks. His career pressure-to-sack rates were 51st in both 2023 and 2025, so this is a long-standing trait, not a new flaw. It is the price of a 3.11-second time to throw and of looking for scramble lanes. The scrambles pay much of it back, but a line ranked 24th in hit rate allowed doesn't help.

concerns.title: Third down and red zone flat
concerns.body: On third down he converted 34.8% with average EPA near zero, facing an average of 9.2 yards to go, so the down-and-distance did him no favors. In the red zone he produced four touchdowns but a negative CPOE and no net EPA. These splits sit on 23 and 15 plays, so they read as noise far more than as a flaw, especially given how well he threw everywhere else.

trend.note: His efficiency climbed through September: the Week 2 loss to New Orleans was the low point, followed by two near-identical 10-EPA outings against Dallas and Tennessee. Then the season broke on availability: half a game in Week 4, three missed starts, and a one-throw Week 8 exit before surgery.

nextGame.headline: Jackson won't play; Huntley inherits a soft Carolina pass rush.
nextGame.body:
Jackson is on injured reserve and will not face Carolina. Huntley has started three of the past six weeks and is the likely starter. On paper the matchup would have suited Jackson's game. Carolina ranks last in both sack rate and QB hit rate, which would cut into his biggest weakness, the sacks that come from holding the ball. Its pass defense ranks 23rd in EPA. The catch is that Carolina allows the second-lowest explosive pass rate and holds lead receivers down, ranking 4th in EPA allowed to WR1s, while tight ends have found room.

Availability on the Carolina side favors whoever takes the snaps for Baltimore. Cornerbacks Will Lee (73% of snaps) and Mike Jackson (69%) and linebacker Bobby Okereke (89%) are all out. For Baltimore, guard Olaivavega Ioane (91% of snaps) left Monday's game with a shoulder injury and was questionable to return, which matters for pass protection whoever plays quarterback. The Ravens are 2.5-point underdogs with a 43.5 total.

keyMatchups.title: No pass rush to speak of
keyMatchups.body: Carolina ranks 32nd in both sack rate and hit rate, so a Baltimore quarterback should have time even with a protection unit ranked 24th in hits allowed. That time is exactly what Jackson's long-developing passing game needs.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted secondary, but few explosives
keyMatchups.body: Two regular corners are out. Even so, Carolina has limited explosive passes (2nd) and held WR1s to 0.09 EPA per target, so Flowers' big-play role is the hardest part of the passing game to replicate. Andrews' tight-end role faces a defense ranked 26th against TE1s.

nextGame.watch: Any update to Jackson's 6-to-10-week timeline, and whether Ioane's shoulder keeps a 91%-snap guard out of the lineup.

restOfSeason.body:
The realistic expectation is a long absence with a possible return around the final stretch of the regular season, if the late-December estimate holds. Nothing he does on the field matters until then, and a 6-to-10-week range means a playoff-only return or a lost season are both on the table. If he comes back, the base skill set looks sound. His 2026 rates line up with his 2019 and 2024 peaks, and his short-area accuracy and scrambling are traits he has shown for years.

What should regress is the edge of the efficiency. A CPOE above 8 and YPA near 10 on 97 attempts sit well above anything in his career, and the deep and intermediate EPA rests on small samples. A returning Jackson in this run-leaning, low-volume offense projects as a very efficient passer rather than a high-volume one: roughly 180-235 passing yards, one to two touchdowns and 20-40 rushing yards a game, with the low end more likely in his first game back.
